claim_boundaries: This file contains deterministic semantic descriptors, not executable AP2, FIDO, WebAuthn, authenticator, merchant-JWS, or payment-provider vectors.
Executable coverage is attributed only through an exact repository test file and exact test title in the test catalog; presence here does not assert that a test passed in any particular run.
A vector may describe only the subcase identified by its coverage.case_scope and must not be read as coverage of every behavior named by the containing test.

Native AP2 verification remains authoritative for mandate SD-JWTs, merchant checkout JWS verification, current-checkout validation, checkout hashing, and CheckoutMandate-to-PaymentMandate transaction linkage.
The WebAuthn adapter verifies only the RP-pinned human-authorization artifact and never implies native AP2 validity.
The closed profile accepts one canonical CheckoutMandate token and one canonical PaymentMandate token for immediate execution only.
The native source binding commits both exact token bytes and both disclosure-resolved payloads; the projected objects must match those authenticated payload commitments.
The WebAuthn signature counter is a durable monotonic admission resource, not merely a comparison with enrollment metadata.
Human evidence acceptance, exact action matching, AEB satisfaction, local authorization, AdmissionStore custody, provider commitment, and observed effect are separate states.
AdmissionStore is the sole authority-custody and one-time boundary; pure bridge builders do not reserve, invoke, or reconcile.
Provider commitment and observed effect are independent axes, including COMMITTED with DIVERGED.
Post-entry ambiguity consumes authority, forbids blind retry, and requires authenticated reconciliation without retransmission.
The profile is one tenant per deployment boundary and makes no FIDO final-standard, FIDO certification, AP2 certification, legal-consent, settlement, or effect-proof claim.

baseline.checkout_payload_jwt_commitment: sha256:<domain-separated exact merchant checkout JWS bytes>

vectors.description: The exact v0.2 CheckoutMandate and PaymentMandate member sets project to one immediate payment action with source expiry.

coverage.case_scope: closed v0.2 model members, transaction linkage, action projection, source expiry

vectors.description: The same two canonical single-token strings produce the same domain-separated commitments and native artifact digest.
Missing or duplicate separators, leading whitespace, or an empty token is refused before projection.
The pre-v0.2 CartMandate and opaque user_authorization shape is not accepted.
An open CheckoutMandate VCT is outside the closed profile.
An open PaymentMandate VCT is outside the closed profile.
A scheduled payment is outside the immediate-only profile.
A recurring payment or an added recurrence member fails the closed member check.
The PaymentMandate cannot be projected when transaction_id differs from CheckoutMandate.checkout_hash.
A source binding whose component commitment no longer matches its native artifact digest is refused.
Mutation of each declared material action field is refused.
Mutation of either mandate token commitment or the native-attestation commitment is refused.

coverage.case_scope: loop over all source commitment fields

vectors.description: Post-signing disclosure, tenant, relying party, operation, effect request, or provider-tuple mutation is refused.
Every source, scope, provider, action, CAID, disclosure, approver, nonce, and expiry context binding is RP-checked.

coverage.case_scope: loop over every signed context binding

vectors.description: The authorization context may not outlive the earlier AP2 source expiry.
An expired CheckoutMandate or PaymentMandate makes the human evidence non-current.
A validly shaped assertion from an unpinned origin is refused.
Authenticator data for another RP ID is refused.
A modified ES256 signature is refused.
A different credential, inactive root, revoked status, or stale status is refused.

coverage.case_scope: credential, root-status, revoked-status, and stale-status fixtures

vectors.description: The closed human leg requires both UP and UV.
A counter not strictly above the enrolled counter is refused.
BE or BS is refused when the RP-pinned policy disallows it.
The no-extension profile refuses authenticator data beyond 37 bytes.
A separately valid exact effect context receives a distinct replay unit.

coverage.case_scope: operation, request digest, and provider tuple variants

vectors.description: Successful WebAuthn verification does not convert an expected-action mismatch into a match.
An unpinned mapping profile is indeterminate and yields no CAID.
The commitment-only human artifact rejects embedded raw AP2 mandates.
Unknown fields, oversized client data, poisoned arrays, non-JSON values, and empty identifiers fail closed.

coverage.case_scope: unknown, oversized, poisoned, non-JSON, and empty-operation fixtures

vectors.description: Separate AP2-native and WebAuthn-human legs compose to SATISFIED and re-verify in execution mode.

The builder uses current mandates, exact source tokens, and trusted controls to derive three replay resources, one monotonic-counter resource, one provider-operation resource, and two external leases without reserving them.

coverage.case_scope: canonical snapshot, exact source projection, request digest, replay resources, monotonic counter, provider operation, and two status leases

vectors.description: The AEB AdmissionInput retains the digest of the complete signed evaluation record and composes with qualification, AEC, and local policy for one snapshot.

coverage.case_scope: complete evaluation record digest and qualification bundle composition

vectors.description: Request-side clock, pinned configuration, current status, status resolver, or provider verifier fields are refused.
A forged signed AEB evaluation is not execution-authorizing.
A server-owned initiator or executor mismatch with the signed AEB record is refused.
The pinned provider-request verifier receives the exact request bytes, PaymentMandate token, token digest, and provider tuple.
A one-byte request mutation is refused when its recomputed digest differs from the signed Gate binding.
An alternate PaymentMandate token is refused even if a presenter-supplied verifier callback returns true.
A provider-request verifier whose implementation digest differs from the executor-adapter digest is refused.
Admission is refused when the pinned adapter cannot establish exact PaymentMandate-token binding in the provider request.
Wrong status artifact identity, wrong evidence digest, expired source authority, or admission outliving source authority is refused.

coverage.case_scope: all status identity, evidence digest, source expiry, and admission expiry fixtures

vectors.description: An otherwise valid assertion is refused when its signCount does not advance beyond the server-owned credential head.
Only the exact expected-to-next counter transition reserves; duplicate counts conflict, later counts advance, and an earlier reserved admission remains invocable.
